newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss franc closes softer, dollar pressure remains.
newsitem.headline: Swiss franc closes softer, dollar pressure remains.

text.p: 1550 GMT - The Swiss franc ended weaker against the dollar and mark, with some traders seeing technicals pointing to further strength for the dollar.
The dollar's ability to hold above 1.4330 francs at the close on Wednesday led to technical buying on Thursday.

"At the closing we had a pretty high level... so that led to buying," said Aurel David, technical currency analyst at Bank Julius Baer. If the dollar support holds, it could next target 1.4519 and 1.4710 francs, he said.

David said that the dollar may be primed for a major move to 1.4950 francs longer-term. The dollar also may be still gaining on orders from participants who missed the dollar's rally, and were looking to buy on pullbacks.

The Swiss franc got no lasting gain from news that the Swiss National Bank left interest rates steady, amidst scattered speculation from a few dealers that the rate may be cut at Thursday's SNB board meeting. The franc only briefly edged higher against the dollar after the SNB news. But it ultimately ended below afternoon levels where it traded before the SNB left rates unchanged.
The Swiss franc made slight headway against the mark after the SNB left rates steady, but it also ended lower against the German currency.
* The dollar ended at 1.4493/4498 Swiss francs versus 1.4455/4465 francs at the close on Wednesday.
* The mark ended at 85.92/95 Swiss centimes versus 85.88/92 centimes on Wednesday.
